correctness.rationale: Every commuting tuple gives a unique orthogonal 2^k-color joint-image decomposition, and conversely; automorphism transitivity with product stabilizers yields the exact integral summands. The automorphism order follows by counting all homomorphisms and using the block-upper-triangular criterion on G/pG. Möbius inversion yields the clique polynomial; indecomposable refinement yields maximal cliques and their stabilizer. The unique-largest-exponent cancellation is termwise in each orbit quotient. The rank-two graph follows from the two-atom decomposition. An independently implemented finite enumeration checks six small groups at primes 2 and 3 through tuples of length 3 and maximal cliques. Infinite claims rely on the proof, not these checks.

value.rationale: The theorem determines every clique coefficient and every maximal commuting family for endomorphism rings of all finite abelian p-groups, including modules with arbitrarily mixed exponents. It proves that these complete compatibility statistics cannot reconstruct even the order or exponent of a group when the maximal cyclic factor is unique. The invariant-blindness phenomenon is mathematically motivated by distinguishing direct-summand compatibility from full ring or group structure; the p=2 rank-three example is not covered by the homogeneous local-ring matrix count.
